style_when: the story is about change after hours — automation displacing shifts, a market open all night, capacity running while people sleep
prompt: Architectural photograph of a residential home at blue hour, asymmetric off-centre composition. The original dark suburban house sits in deep blue ambient shadow on the left, while a newly constructed, modern timber and glass addition on the right wing glows intensely with warm amber interior lighting. 35mm anamorphic wide lens, crisp atmospheric depth, long-exposure calm with no moving figures, deep shadows, clean architectural geometry, premium editorial cover standard.
negative_prompt: text, letters, numbers, watermark, UI, typography, garbled, blurred
rationale: Architectural night perfectly captures the physical reality of a home addition. By lighting the new wing brightly against the dark original structure, it visually represents the distinct, uncapped 'new value' attaching to the permanent base.
cue: enters the roll at full value
subject: a newly constructed modern home addition glowing warmly alongside a dark older house
core_thesis: Assessment caps limit tax drift on an existing home, but newly built additions are assessed at full market value immediately upon completion.
core_conflict: capped historical property base vs uncapped new addition value
